subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse note (not a proof step): cbr_ci_density_representation is a comparator-accepted DAG declaration, reused here under its own name with its byte-identical frozen type; the argument below is re-derived from the parent's Step 3 and is given for completeness.
Source: parent proof, Step 3 (representation of Γ; parent V6), items (a)–(e).
1. Dual norm. For an n-vector ζ put |ζ|* := sup{ζ(β) : |β| ≤ 1}. The space of n-covectors is finite dimensional and covectorEuclideanNorm is a norm on it (if all coefficients α(e_{i_1}, …, e_{i_n}), i_1 < ⋯ < i_n, vanish then α = 0 by multilinearity and alternation), so its closed unit ball is compact and the supremum is attained; |·|* is a norm on Λ_n (hence continuous), |ζ(α)| ≤ |ζ|*|α|, and |ζ|* ≤ 1 iff |ζ(α)| ≤ |α| for all α. (If n > P all n-covectors vanish, Λ_n = 0, Γ = 0, μ = 0 and M := ∅ works.)
2. |ξ|* = 1 μ-a.e. (Step 3(a)). x ↦ |ξ(x)|* is μ-a.e. measurable with values in [0, 1]. For ω admissible for M_{ℝ^P}(Γ) (|ω(x)| ≤ 1 everywhere), Γ(ω) = ∫ξ(x)(ω(x))dμ ≤ ∫|ξ(x)|*|ω(x)|dμ ≤ ∫|ξ|*dμ. Hence μ(ℝ^P) = M_{ℝ^P}(Γ) ≤ ∫|ξ|*dμ ≤ μ(ℝ^P) < ∞, so ∫(1 − |ξ|*)dμ = 0 with 1 − |ξ|* ≥ 0, i.e. |ξ|* = 1 μ-a.e.
3. Borel normalized field (Step 3(b)). Choose ξ₀ strongly measurable with ξ = ξ₀ μ-a.e. and set ζ(x) := ξ₀(x)/max(1, |ξ₀(x)|*). ζ is strongly measurable (continuous function of ξ₀), |ζ(x)|* ≤ 1, i.e. |ζ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all x, α, and ζ = ξ₀ wherever |ξ₀|* ≤ 1, in particular wherever ξ₀ = ξ; so ζ = ξ μ-a.e., Γ(ω) = ∫ζ(ω)dμ for all ω and |ζ|* = 1 μ-a.e.
4. The density set (Step 3(c)). Θ(x) := liminf_{r↓0}μ(B_r(x))/(ω_nrⁿ). S := {x : Θ(x) < η₀} is μ-null; let N₁ := toMeasurable μ S (a Borel superset with μ(N₁) = 0) and M₀ := ℝ^P∖N₁: Borel, μ(ℝ^P∖M₀) = 0 and Θ ≥ η₀ on M₀.
5. Hⁿ(M₀) < ∞ (a non-sharp Vitali argument suffices). For x ∈ M₀ and all small ρ > 0, μ(B̄_ρ(x)) ≥ μ(B_ρ(x)) ≥ (η₀/2)ω_nρⁿ. Fix δ > 0 and let 𝓑 be the family of closed balls B̄_ρ(x) with x ∈ M₀, 0 < ρ < δ and μ(B̄_ρ(x)) ≥ (η₀/2)ω_nρⁿ; it covers M₀ finely. By the Vitali 5r-covering lemma (Mathlib Vitali.exists_disjoint_subfamily_covering_enlargement_closedBall) there is a disjoint subfamily (B̄_{ρ_i}(x_i))_{i∈I} with M₀ ⊆ ⋃_iB̄_{5ρ_i}(x_i); I is countable (disjoint balls of positive μ-measure, μ finite). Then Σ_i(10ρ_i)ⁿ ≤ (2·10ⁿ/(η₀ω_n))Σ_iμ(B̄_{ρ_i}(x_i)) ≤ 2·10ⁿμ(ℝ^P)/(η₀ω_n) =: Λ < ∞, and diam B̄_{5ρ_i}(x_i) ≤ 10δ. By the definition of μH[n] (Measure.hausdorffMeasure_le_liminf_tsum along δ → 0), μH[n](M₀) ≤ Λ, hence Hⁿ(M₀) = c_n·μH[n](M₀) < ∞ with the finite constant c_n of euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def. (The parent's Step 0(e) gives the sharper Hⁿ(M₀) ≤ 2μ(ℝ^P)/η₀; finiteness is all that is used.)
6. Radon–Nikodym (Step 3(d)). ν₀ := Hⁿ⌞M₀ is finite and μ ≪ ν₀: if Hⁿ(E ∩ M₀) = 0 then μ(E ∩ M₀) = 0 by hypothesis and μ(E∖M₀) ≤ μ(ℝ^P∖M₀) = 0 (for non-measurable E use a measurable superset). By the Lebesgue decomposition μ = μ.singularPart ν₀ + ν₀.withDensity(μ.rnDeriv ν₀) (Measure.haveLebesgueDecomposition_add) and μ.singularPart ν₀ = 0 (Measure.singularPart_eq_zero_of_ac), so μ = ν₀.withDensity h with h := μ.rnDeriv ν₀ measurable, [0, ∞]-valued, h < ∞ ν₀-a.e. (Measure.rnDeriv_lt_top) and ∫_{M₀}h dHⁿ = μ(ℝ^P) < ∞.
7. The carrier (Step 3(e)). M := M₀ ∩ {0 < h < ∞} ∩ {|ζ|* = 1}, Borel. μ(ℝ^P∖M) = 0: μ(ℝ^P∖M₀) = 0; μ(M₀ ∩ {h = 0}) = ∫_{M₀∩{h=0}}h dHⁿ = 0; ν₀{h = ∞} = 0 hence μ{h = ∞} = 0; μ{|ζ|* ≠ 1} = 0 (step 3). Hⁿ(M) ≤ Hⁿ(M₀) < ∞. Put θ := (1_M·h).toReal: Borel, θ > 0 on M and ofReal(θ(x)) = h(x) for x ∈ M.
8. μ = (Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity(ofReal∘θ): for Borel E, μ(E) = μ(E ∩ M) = ∫_{E∩M}h d(Hⁿ⌞M₀) = ∫_{E∩M}ofReal(θ)dHⁿ (M ⊆ M₀).
9. Representation. Γ(ω) = ∫ζ(ω)dμ = ∫ζ(ω)d((Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity(ofReal∘θ)) = ∫_M(ofReal θ).toReal·ζ(ω)dHⁿ = ∫_Mθ(x)ζ(x)(ω(x))dHⁿ(x) (integral_withDensity_eq_integral_toReal_smul; (ofReal θ).toReal = θ as θ ≥ 0).
10. Pointwise properties on M: θ > 0 (step 7); |ζ(x)|* = 1, so by step 1 some β with |β| ≤ 1 has ζ(x)(β) = 1; |ζ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| everywhere (step 3); Θ(x) ≥ η₀ (M ⊆ M₀, step 4). With Hⁿ(M) < ∞, θ Borel and ζ strongly measurable, all assertions hold. ∎
proof_key_steps: |ξ|* = 1 μ-a.e. because μ(ℝ^P) = M(Γ) ≤ ∫|ξ|*dμ; replace ξ by a Borel normalized ζ.
M₀ := complement of a Borel μ-null set containing {Θ < η₀}; a Vitali covering gives Hⁿ(M₀) < ∞.
μ ≪ Hⁿ⌞M₀; the Lebesgue decomposition gives the density h; carrier M := M₀ ∩ {0 < h < ∞} ∩ {|ζ|* = 1}, θ := h.toReal.
Transfer Γ(ω) = ∫ζ(ω)dμ to Γ(ω) = ∫_Mθζ(ω)dHⁿ and read off the pointwise properties on M.

4. (Mass bound.) Let k ∈ ℕ, R > 0 and G open with G ⊆ B̄_R(0). Then M_G(X_k) ≤ ofReal(s)·ν_k(G) + ofReal(Pⁿ)·δ_k(R). By definition M_G(X_k) is the supremum of ofReal(X_k(ω)) over ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn univ n G, i.e. tsupport ω̂ ⊆ G and |ω̂(x)| ≤ 1 for all x; fix such ω (sSup_le). By the sibling covector_norm (cbr_ci_bl_covector_opNorm_le), ‖ω̂(x)‖ ≤ Pⁿ|ω̂(x)| ≤ Pⁿ for all x, and tsupport ω̂ ⊆ B̄_R(0). If ofReal(Pⁿ)·δ_k(R) = ∞ the bound is trivial. Otherwise step 2 with A = Pⁿ gives X_k(ω) = ∫ f_ω dν_k + ∫ g_{k,ω} dν_k and ∫ g_{k,ω} dν_k ≤ (ofReal(Pⁿ)·δ_k(R)).toReal. Moreover f_ω(x) ≤ |ζ₀(ω̂(x))| ≤ s|ω̂(x)| ≤ s for x ∈ G and f_ω(x) = 0 for x ∉ G, i.e. f_ω ≤ 1_G·s; as ν_k(G) ≤ ν_k(B̄_R(0)) < ∞, 1_G·s is integrable (integrableOn_const, IntegrableOn.integrable_indicator), so ∫ f_ω dν_k ≤ s·ν_k(G).toReal (integral_mono, integral_indicator_const). Therefore ofReal(X_k(ω)) ≤ ofReal(s·ν_k(G).toReal) + ofReal((ofReal(Pⁿ)·δ_k(R)).toReal) = ofReal(s)·ν_k(G) + ofReal(Pⁿ)·δ_k(R) (ENNReal.ofReal_add_le, ENNReal.ofReal_mul with s ≥ 0, ENNReal.ofReal_toReal).
5. (One thickening.) Let K be compact and r > 0. G_r := thickening r K is open with K ⊆ G_r ⊆ K_r := cthickening r K (self_subset_thickening, thickening_subset_cthickening), and K_r is compact (IsCompact.cthickening); choose R > 0 with K_r ⊆ B̄_R(0). By monotonicity of μ_k, the mass hypothesis and step 4, μ_k(K) ≤ μ_k(G_r) = M_{G_r}(X_k) ≤ ofReal(s)·ν_k(K_r) + v_k for all k, where v_k := ofReal(Pⁿ)·δ_k(R) → 0. Also limsup_k ofReal(s)·ν_k(K_r) = ofReal(s)·limsup_k ν_k(K_r) ≤ ofReal(s)·ν(K_r) (ENNReal.limsup_const_mul_of_ne_top and the hypothesis on compact sets). Claim: limsup_k μ_k(K) ≤ ofReal(s)·ν(K_r). Let c > ofReal(s)·ν(K_r) and pick b with ofReal(s)·ν(K_r) < b < c (exists_between). Eventually ofReal(s)·ν_k(K_r) < b (eventually_lt_of_limsup_lt) and eventually v_k < c − b (v_k → 0 and c − b > 0, tendsto_order), so eventually μ_k(K) ≤ b + (c − b) = c; hence limsup_k μ_k(K) ≤ c (limsup_le_of_le), and as c was arbitrary the claim follows (le_of_forall_gt_imp_ge_of_dense). (This route avoids ENNReal.limsup_add_le, which needs a countable-intersection filter.)
6. (Letting r ↓ 0.) K is closed and ν(K_1) < ∞ (K_1 compact), so ν(K_r) → ν(K) as r → 0 (tendsto_measure_cthickening_of_isClosed) and hence ofReal(s)·ν(K_r) → ofReal(s)·ν(K) along 𝓝[>] 0 (ENNReal.Tendsto.const_mul, ofReal(s) < ∞). Since limsup_k μ_k(K) ≤ ofReal(s)·ν(K_r) for every r > 0 by step 5, ge_of_tendsto gives limsup_k μ_k(K) ≤ ofReal(s)·ν(K). Together with step 3 this proves both conclusions. ∎

1. (The map and the rescaled mass measure.) η = D as functions (unfold blowUpMap, dilation, dilationCLM; smul_sub; abel). D is the homeomorphism e := (y ↦ λ⁻¹y) followed by (z ↦ −λ⁻¹a + z) (Homeomorph.smulOfNeZero, Homeomorph.addLeft), so D is a measurable embedding, surjective and injective, and a + λ·D(x) = x for every x. By the sibling blowup_measure (cbr_ci_bl_blowUp_restrict_scaling) applied to M, θ, a, λ: η(M) is Borel, and (part (iii), after rewriting μ by its hypothesis) μ' = c·D_#((Hⁿ⌞M) with density ofReal∘θ) = (Hⁿ⌞η(M)) with density y ↦ ofReal θ(a + λy).
2. (P0.) For a test n-form ω: since x ↦ ofReal θ(x) is measurable and finite, ∫ ζ(x)(ω̂(x)) dμ = ∫ (ofReal θ(x)).toReal·ζ(x)(ω̂(x)) d(Hⁿ⌞M) (integral_withDensity_eq_integral_toReal_smul). For x ∈ M, θ(x) > 0, so (ofReal θ(x)).toReal = θ(x) (ENNReal.toReal_ofReal); as M is Borel, setIntegral_congr_fun turns the last integral into ∫_M θ(x)·ζ(x)(ω̂(x)) dHⁿ, which equals Γ(ω) by hypothesis.
3. (P7.) Let ω be a test d-form and ω' := ω̂∘D. ω' is smooth, because ω̂ is smooth and D = (constant) + dilationCLM P λ is C^∞ (ContDiff.comp, contDiff_const.add, ContinuousLinearMap.contDiff), and it has compact support (HasCompactSupport.comp_homeomorph with e, since e = D); trivially tsupport ω' ⊆ ℝ^P. So ω' is a test d-form with ω'(y) = ω̂(D(y)) for all y, and (h2) gives ∂Γ'(ω) = λ^{−d}·∂Γ(ω') = λ^{−d}·0 = 0. Hence ∂Γ' = 0 (GeometricCurrentOn.ext, GeometricCurrentOn.zero_apply).
4. (P1.) For every K: μ'(K) = c·μ(D⁻¹K) (Measure.smul_apply, MeasurableEmbedding.map_apply) ≤ c·μ(ℝ^P) < ∞, as c < ∞ and μ(ℝ^P) < ∞ (ENNReal.mul_lt_top).
5. (P2.) Let W be open. W₀ := D⁻¹(W) is open (D is continuous) and D(W₀) = W (Set.image_preimage_eq, D surjective). By (h5) and the mass hypothesis for Γ: M_W(Γ') = M_{D(W₀)}(Γ') = c·M_{W₀}(Γ) = c·μ(W₀) = c·μ(D⁻¹W) = μ'(W) (Measure.smul_apply, MeasurableEmbedding.map_apply).
6. (P3.) y ↦ a + λy is measurable, so y ↦ ζ(a + λy) is strongly measurable (StronglyMeasurable.comp_measurable), hence μ'-a.e. strongly measurable.
7. (P5.) Apply (h4) to (P0).
8. (P6.) μ'(η(M)ᶜ) = c·μ(D⁻¹(η(M)ᶜ)) (MeasurableEmbedding.map_apply), and D⁻¹(η(M)ᶜ) = (D⁻¹(D(M)))ᶜ = Mᶜ (Set.preimage_compl, η = D, Function.Injective.preimage_image). Further μ(Mᶜ) = ∫⁻_{Mᶜ} ofReal θ d(Hⁿ⌞M) (withDensity_apply, Mᶜ Borel) = 0, because (Hⁿ⌞M)⌞Mᶜ = Hⁿ⌞(Mᶜ ∩ M) = Hⁿ⌞∅ = 0 (Measure.restrict_restrict, compl_inter_self, Measure.restrict_empty, lintegral_zero_measure). So μ'(η(M)ᶜ) = c·0 = 0.

By (P5) and step 1, Γ'(ω) = ∫ ζ(a + λy)(ω̂(y)) d((Hⁿ⌞η(M)) with density ofReal θ(a + λ·)) = ∫_{η(M)} (ofReal θ(a + λy)).toReal·ζ(a + λy)(ω̂(y)) dHⁿ(y) (integral_withDensity_eq_integral_toReal_smul; y ↦ ofReal θ(a + λy) is measurable and finite). For y ∈ η(M), y = η(x) with x ∈ M, and a + λy = a + λD(x) = x, so (ofReal θ(a + λy)).toReal = θ(x) = θ(a + λy) and the integrand equals (θ(a + λy)·ζ(a + λy))(ω̂(y)) (ContinuousLinearMap.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul). Fact (O) (parent Step 0(a); orthogonal invariance of the coefficient norm). For an orthonormal basis f = (f_1, …, f_P) of ℝ^P and a k-covector α, Σ_{j : Fin k → Fin P}α(f_{j(1)}, …, f_{j(k)})² = k!·|α|²: write f_i = Σ_lO_{li}e_l with O orthogonal and expand α(f_{j(1)}, …, f_{j(k)}) = Σ_lO_{l_1j(1)}⋯O_{l_kj(k)}α(e_{l_1}, …, e_{l_k}); summing the squares over j and using Σ_iO_{li}O_{l'i} = δ_{ll'} gives Σ_{l : Fin k → Fin P}α(e_l)², where non-injective l contribute 0 and each increasing multi-index I contributes k! equal terms α(e_I)². Consequences: (O1) if v = (v_1, …, v_k) is orthonormal then |α(v)| ≤ |α| (extend v to an orthonormal basis; the k! permutations of (1, …, k) already contribute k!α(v)²); (O2) β_v(u) := det(⟨u_i, v_j⟩)_{i,j} is a k-covector (multilinear and alternating in u) with β_v(v) = 1 and |β_v| = 1 (in a basis extending v its only non-zero values are ±1 on the permutations of (1, …, k)); (O3) if p : ℝ^P → ℝ^k, p(x) := (⟨x, v_1⟩, …, ⟨x, v_k⟩) with v orthonormal, then the pulled-back covector p^#γ := γ∘(p × ⋯ × p) of an l-covector γ on ℝ^k has |p^#γ| = |γ| (in a basis f extending v, p(f_i) = e_i for i ≤ k and p(f_i) = 0 otherwise, so the sums of (O) for p^#γ and γ coincide).
0. Notation. For w ∈ ℝ^P let w^♭ := ⟨w, ·⟩. For a d-covector α (a real number if d = 0) let w^♭∧α be the n-covector (u_1, …, u_n) ↦ Σ_j(−1)^{j−1}⟨w, u_j⟩α(u_1, …, û_j, …, u_n) (for d = 0: α⟨w, u_1⟩). w ↦ ζ₀(w^♭∧α) is linear; let v_α ∈ ℝ^P be its Riesz representative: ⟨v_α, w⟩ = ζ₀(w^♭∧α).
1. Directional identity. For φ ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ^P) and a fixed d-covector α, the test d-form φα : y ↦ φ(y)α has d(φα)(y) = (∇φ(y))^♭∧α (exteriorDerivative_apply: the alternating sum of the directional derivatives Dφ(y)[u_j]α(…û_j…)). By (1), 0 = ∫ζ₀((∇φ)^♭∧α)dν = ∫⟨v_α, ∇φ⟩dν = ∫Dφ(y)[v_α]dν(y).
2. Translation invariance. Fix α, v := v_α, φ ∈ C_c^∞ and F(s) := ∫φ(y + sv)dν(y). For s in a bounded interval the functions y ↦ φ(y + sv), y ↦ Dφ(y + sv)[v] are bounded and supported in a fixed compact set (of finite ν-measure), so F is differentiable with F'(s) = ∫Dφ(y + sv)[v]dν(y) = 0 by step 1 applied to φ(· + sv) ∈ C_c^∞. Hence ∫φ(y + sv)dν = ∫φ dν for all s and φ ∈ C_c^∞, hence for all φ ∈ C_c (uniform approximation by mollification with supports in a fixed compact set). The translate of ν by sv and ν are Borel measures finite on compact sets with the same integrals of all of C_c, so they are equal (Measure.ext_of_integral_eq_on_compactlySupported). Composing translations, ν is invariant under translation by every vector of V₀ := span{v_α : α a d-covector}.
3. Only coordinates inside V₀ matter. Let r := dim V₀ and choose an orthonormal basis e'_1, …, e'_P of ℝ^P with V₀ = span(e'_1, …, e'_r). Every n-covector expands as β = Σ_Iβ(e'_I)e'^I over increasing multi-indices I, e'^I := e'^{i_1♭}∧⋯∧e'^{i_n♭}. If I contains some i > r then e'^I = ±e'^{i♭}∧e'^{I∖i} and ζ₀(e'^I) = ±⟨v_{e'^{I∖i}}, e'_i⟩ = 0, because v_{e'^{I∖i}} ∈ V₀ ⊥ e'_i. So ζ₀(β) = Σ_{I⊆{1..r}}β(e'_I)ζ₀(e'^I) for all β. As ζ₀(β₁) = 1 ≠ 0, some increasing I ⊆ {1, …, r} with n elements exists: r ≥ n.
4. Growth forces r ≤ n. By (3), m₀ := ν(B_1(0)) > 0, and by step 2, ν(B_1(u)) = m₀ for every u ∈ V₀. For R ≥ 4 consider u = 2Σ_{j≤r}k_je'_j with k ∈ ℤ^r, |k_j| ≤ R/(4√r): these points are at mutual distance ≥ 2 and |u| ≤ R/2, so the balls B_1(u) are pairwise disjoint and contained in B_R(0); there are at least c_rR^r of them for some c_r > 0. Hence c_rm₀R^r ≤ ν(B_R(0)) ≤ ω_nRⁿ (by (2)) for all large R, which forces r ≤ n. So r = n, V₀ = span(e'_1, …, e'_n) and, by step 3, ζ₀(β) = s·β(e'_1, …, e'_n) with s := ζ₀(e'^{(1,…,n)}).
5. Normalisation. For the orthonormal v := (e'_1, …, e'_n), (O1) gives |β(v)| ≤ |β| for all β and (O2) gives β₂ := β_v with |β₂| = 1, β₂(v) = 1. Thus |s| = |ζ₀(β₂)| ≤ 1 and 1 = ζ₀(β₁) = sβ₁(v) ≤ |s||β₁| ≤ |s|, so |s| = 1. If s = −1 replace e'_1 by −e'_1 (still orthonormal, same span; β(v) changes sign). Hence ζ₀(β) = β(v_1, …, v_n) for all β, with v orthonormal and span(v) = V₀.
6. Product structure (Step 7(a)). Write ℝ^P = V₀ ⊕ V₀^⊥. For a bounded Borel B ⊆ V₀^⊥, A ↦ ν(A + B) (A ⊆ V₀ Borel; A + B is Borel as the image of A × B under the linear isomorphism V₀ × V₀^⊥ → ℝ^P) is a translation-invariant Borel measure on V₀ (step 2), finite on compact sets. V₀ is isometric to ℝⁿ with Hⁿ⌞V₀ corresponding to Lebesgue measure (Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure, EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume), so by uniqueness of Haar measure (Measure.isAddLeftInvariant_eq_smul) ν(A + B) = σ(B)Hⁿ(A) with σ(B) := ν((V₀ ∩ B_1(0)) + B)/ω_n. Defining σ(B) by this formula for all Borel B ⊆ V₀^⊥ gives a Borel measure on V₀^⊥, finite on bounded sets, with ν(A + B) = Hⁿ(A)σ(B) for all Borel A ⊆ V₀, B ⊆ V₀^⊥. The sets A + B form a π-system generating the Borel sets of ℝ^P on which ν and (Hⁿ⌞V₀) ⊗ σ (transported to ℝ^P) agree, both finite on the sets (V₀ ∩ B_j(0)) + (V₀^⊥ ∩ B_j(0)) covering ℝ^P; hence ν = (Hⁿ⌞V₀) ⊗ σ (Measure.ext_of_generateFrom_of_iUnion).
7. σ is purely atomic with atoms ≥ c (Step 7(b)). For y = u + w (u ∈ V₀, w ∈ V₀^⊥), B_r(y) ⊆ (V₀ ∩ B_r(u)) + (V₀^⊥ ∩ B_r(w)), so ν(B_r(y)) ≤ ω_nrⁿσ(B_r(w)). By (4), for ν-a.e. y: c ≤ liminf_{r↓0}ν(B_r(y))/(ω_nrⁿ) ≤ liminf_{r↓0}σ(B_r(w)) = σ({w}) (continuity from above, σ(B_1(w)) < ∞). The set Z := {w ∈ V₀^⊥ : σ({w}) ≥ c} is locally finite (a bounded B contains at most σ(B)/c of its points), hence closed and countable, and G := V₀^⊥∖Z is Borel. V₀ + G is ν-null by the preceding sentence, so ω_nσ(G) = ν((V₀ ∩ B_1(0)) + G) = 0. Hence σ = Σ_{w∈Z}σ({w})δ_w.
8. Finitely many planes with Σα_i ≤ 1 (Step 7(c)). Enumerate Z = {w_i} and put α_i := σ({w_i}) ≥ c; then ν = Σ_iα_iHⁿ⌞(V₀ + w_i) (step 6). For R > 0, since w_i ⊥ V₀, (V₀ + w_i) ∩ B_R(0) is an n-ball of radius (R² − |w_i|²)_+^{1/2} in the plane V₀ + w_i, so ν(B_R(0)) = Σ_iα_iω_n(R² − |w_i|²)_+^{n/2}. By (2), for every finite subfamily F, Σ_{i∈F}α_i(1 − |w_i|²/R²)_+^{n/2} ≤ 1; letting R → ∞ gives Σ_{i∈F}α_i ≤ 1. As α_i ≥ c > 0, Z is finite, N := #Z ≤ 1/c, and Σ_{i≤N}α_i ≤ 1. The w_i are pairwise distinct and lie in V₀^⊥, i.e. ⟨w_i, v_j⟩ = 0.
9. Some w_i = 0. The support of ν is ⋃_i(V₀ + w_i) (a finite union of planes, each the support of Hⁿ⌞(V₀ + w_i)). By (3), 0 lies in the support of ν, so 0 ∈ V₀ + w_i for some i, i.e. w_i ∈ V₀ ∩ V₀^⊥ = {0}.
10. In the required form: V₀ + w_i = {y : y − w_i ∈ span(v)}, ν = Σ_{i : Fin N}ofReal(α_i)·Hⁿ⌞{y : y − w_i ∈ span(v)}, with α_i ≥ c, Σα_i ≤ 1 and ζ₀(β) = β(v) for all β. ∎

Smooth cut-offs. For a compact K contained in an open Ω ⊆ ℝ^m there is χ ∈ C_c^∞(Ω; [0, 1]) with χ = 1 on an open neighbourhood of K (cover K by finitely many balls B(x, r_x) with B̄(x, 3r_x) ⊆ Ω, take bumps ψ_x ∈ C_c^∞(B(x, 2r_x); [0, 1]) equal to 1 on B(x, r_x) (ContDiffBump) and χ := h∘Σ_xψ_x with h smooth, h(0) = 0, h = 1 on [1, ∞)).

0. Set-up. Fix i₀; α := α_{i₀}, w := w_{i₀}. 2. Slicing (parent Step 8(b)).
